theory: The first fact incorrectly makes the north–south reference compulsory: the booklet also uses the complementary angle from east or west, including its worked example at lines 890–901. State that the triangle angle may be measured from either perpendicular cardinal side, with the ratio chosen accordingly; describe the four listed quadrant formulas specifically as angles from north or south. Also qualify 'acute angle' for cardinal bearings, where the reference angle can be zero or a right angle and the journey has no non-degenerate component triangle.
